title: Unramifiedness at a rational point is surjectivity on cotangent spaces
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a morphism locally of finite type between schemes over a field k [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let x\in X and y=f(x) be closed points with residue fields equal to k. Then f is unramified at x [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if the induced k-linear map on cotangent spaces [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] \mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2\to\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2 is surjective.

source.place: Varieties, lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified, together with the local characterization of unramified morphisms by vanishing relative differentials

proof.text: Choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni y$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\ni x$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and $R\to B$ of finite type (possible since $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]); let $\mathfrak p\subset R$, $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be the primes of $y$, $x$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $C=\mathcal O_{X,x}=B_{\mathfrak q}$, so $A\to C$ is a local homomorphism of local $k$-algebras with $\kappa(y)=\kappa(x)=k$, and the cotangent map of the statement is the induced map $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2\to\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_C^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{C/R}\cong(\Omega_{B/R})_{\mathfrak q}$; and $\Omega_{C/R}=\Omega_{C/A}$, since every $R$-derivation $D$ of $C$ kills $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ ($D(r/s)=s^{-2}(s\,D(r)-r\,D(s))=0$ for $r\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$) and so is an $A$-derivation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Varieties, lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified, affine-local reduction in the proof

proof.text: $f$ is unramified at $x$ (some open neighbourhood of $x$ on which $f$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]) if and only if $\Omega_{C/A}=0$. Indeed $\Omega_{B/R}$ is a finite $B$-module (generated by $\mathrm db_1,\dots,\mathrm db_n$ for $R$-algebra generators $b_i$ of $B$). If $\Omega_{C/A}=(\Omega_{B/R})_{\mathfrak q}=0$ (Step 1), there is $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $(\Omega_{B/R})_g=0$, so $\Omega_{B_g/R}=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], and $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] ($B_g$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra); hence so is $f$ on the open $D(g)\ni x$, since $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ is the restriction of $f$ and $V\to Y$ is an open immersion. Conversely, if $f$ is unramified on an open $W\ni x$, choose $g\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $D(g)\subseteq W\cap U$; then $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is unramified (its diagonal is the diagonal of $f|_{D(g)}$, an open subscheme of $X\times_Y X$ mapping into the open $V\times_V V$), so $\Omega_{B_g/R}=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine], and localizing gives $\Omega_{C/A}=0$. In both cases $\Omega_{C/A}$ is a finite $C$-module.

proof.text: $\Omega_{C/A}\otimes_Ck=0$ if and only if $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_A^2\to\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_C^2$ is surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $A\to C$ and the ideal $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m_C$, with quotient $C/\mathfrak m_C=k$: since $A\to k$ is surjective, $\Omega_{k/A}=0$, so $\delta:\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_C^2\to k\otimes_C\Omega_{C/A}$, $\bar c\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dc$, is surjective. Its kernel contains the image of $\mathfrak m_A$ (as $\mathrm d$ kills $A$), and equals it: let $\lambda:C\to k\subseteq C$ be the residue map (a $k$-algebra map with $k\to C\to k$ the identity, as $\kappa(x)=k$ and $C$ is a $k$-algebra) and put $D(c)=c-\lambda(c)$ modulo $N=\mathfrak m_AC+\mathfrak m_C^2$, a map $C\to\mathfrak m_C/N$. Then $D$ is an $A$-derivation into the $C$-module $\mathfrak m_C/N$: $bc-\lambda(b)\lambda(c)=(b-\lambda b)(c-\lambda c)+\lambda(b)(c-\lambda c)+\lambda(c)(b-\lambda b)$ with the first term in $\mathfrak m_C^2$, and for $a\in A$ one has $a-\lambda(a)\in\mathfrak m_A$. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it induces a $C$-linear map $\Omega_{C/A}\to\mathfrak m_C/N$, which factors through $k\otimes_C\Omega_{C/A}$ since $\mathfrak m_C$ kills $\mathfrak m_C/N$, and whose composite with $\delta$ is the projection $\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_C^2\to\mathfrak m_C/N$. Hence $\ker\delta=N/\mathfrak m_C^2$ and $k\otimes_C\Omega_{C/A}\cong\mathfrak m_C/(\mathfrak m_AC+\mathfrak m_C^2)$, the cokernel of the cotangent map.

proof.text: Since $\Omega_{C/A}$ is a finite module over the local ring $C$, Nakayama's lemma gives $\Omega_{C/A}=0$ if and only if $\Omega_{C/A}\otimes_Ck=0$. With Steps 2 and 3, $f$ is unramified at $x$ if and only if the cotangent map is surjective.

lean.statement: theorem rational_unramified_iff_cotangent_surjective (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) (hy : IsClosed ({f x} : Set Y)) (hκx : Function.Bijective (pX.residueFieldMap x).hom) (hκy : Function.Bijective (pY.residueFieldMap (f x)).hom) : (∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (U.ι ≫ f) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal (U.ι ≫ f))) ↔ Function.Surjective (Ideal.mapCotangent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (f.stalkMap x).hom.toIntAlgHom (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_le (f.stalkMap x).hom)) : IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) →ₗ[ℤ] IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace (X.presheaf.stalk x))
